correctness.rationale: For any positive finite-mean wash-off rate law with mean greater than runoff decay and positive slow-rate mass, H(t)=E exp((gamma-K)t) is strictly convex for t>0, starts at 1 with negative derivative, diverges, and has a unique minimizer. Identity 1-F(v)=(1-v)H(t) gives a global supporting chord with equality only at v* and v=1, while F′ decreases strictly from mu/gamma to c* on [0,v*]. The resulting exact concave envelope proves unique global optimizers in four exhaustive regimes, including both equality endpoints; H(t)=1 has one later root, proving unique flush crossover. Derivatives, expectation exchange, boundary v=1 and infinite-second-moment cases are handled. Exact two-rate witness checked symbolically. Replayed standalone checker produced PASS: 111355 deterministic assertions, supplementary to proof.

originality.rationale: Scoped best-knowledge priority assessment: the recovered full primary article Balistrocchi et al. (2009) uses an event-frequency/Weibull and power-law typical mass-volume construction, while this theorem assumes exponential time-decay runoff, arbitrarily heterogeneous fixed exponential pollutant stocks, and maximizes single-event captured pollutant mass minus cost. Kang (2005) directly motivates two-phase pollutant sources but its inspected erosion model depends on hydraulic mechanics and does not state the universal full/partial/zero capacity threshold. The openly accessible Guo–Urbonas (2000 precursor to 2002 paper) derives rainfall-event depth distribution and basin overflow frequencies rather than within-event pollutant kinetics. published-finding corpus nearest stormwater result has a three-stage stage-ordering threshold, not a storage-capacity optimizer. The complete exact joint classification, not general convex-envelope techniques, is the claim; Millar (1999) and older optimization papers are priority risks due to inaccessible full text.
residual_risks: The full text of Millar (1999) and Fu et al. (2009) could not be inspected; abstract-only comparisons do not rule out related special cases.

Classical concave envelope, exponential mixture and optimal stopping/cost tradeoff literature might include this equivalence under different terminology; priority is necessarily provisional without independent historical review.
Some papers on multi-peak M(V) first/last-flush phenomena concern hydrodynamically richer models and should not be assumed covered by this restricted theorem.

value.rationale: A mass-weighted mixture of fast and slower pollutant stocks gives a motivated departure from standard single power-law within-event mass-volume curves. The theorem gives one exact cost threshold at which a global tank-size optimum jumps discontinuously from the entire storm to a finite first volume with a tied optimum at the boundary, a unique smooth partial branch and exact zero-capture cutoff. This is a natural complete classification across an arbitrary rate law, not an arbitrary special parameter or raw numerical fact; the explicit two-class instance permits checking design heuristics. The same assumptions reveal exactly one first/last flush crossover. Its value is as an analytical stress-test benchmark; no empirical implementation or broad hydrodynamic validity is asserted.
